content.text: – Report of the management board for the period from 1 July to 30 September 2026. Prepared by [PERSON_2], Chief Financial Officer, and approved by [PERSON_1], Chief Executive Officer.
The third quarter of 2026 was the strongest quarter in the history of [ORG_1]. Despite a still hesitant investment climate in the hotel and catering industry, we increased revenue by

compared with the same quarter of the previous year. Order intake grew even faster, by 10.4 percent to EUR 71.2 million, which means that our order backlog reached a new record of EUR 94.6 million at the end of September.
Earnings developed better than revenue. Earnings before interest and taxes (EBIT) rose by 28.3 percent to

, and the EBIT margin improved from 7.3 percent to 8.6 percent. The main drivers were a higher share of service revenue, lower prices for stainless steel sheet compared with the previous year and the first effects of the efficiency programme in our assembly plant in [LOCATION_1].

In the first nine months of the year, revenue amounted to EUR 197.5 million, an increase of 7.2 percent on the prior-year period. EBIT for the nine months was EUR 15.8 million after EUR 13.1 million in the previous year. On the basis of these results and the strong order backlog, we confirm our full-year forecast and now expect to reach the upper half of the forecast range.

The following table compares the key figures of the third quarter with the same quarter of the previous year. All figures are unaudited and prepared in accordance with the German Commercial Code (HGB).

All four segments contributed to the growth in revenue. As in previous quarters, the strongest growth rates came from the service business and from our digital solutions, while the equipment business grew at a more moderate pace.

The Commercial Kitchens segment, which comprises our combi steamers, induction cooking ranges and tilting pans, generated revenue of EUR 38.2 million, an increase of 6.1 percent. Demand from hospitals, care homes and company canteens remained stable, while orders from the hotel industry picked up noticeably after a weak first half of the year. The new generation of combi steamers, launched at the trade fair in May, accounted for around 30 percent of unit sales in this segment in its first full quarter.

Large projects played an important role in the quarter. We delivered the complete kitchen equipment for a new central kitchen of a hospital group in [LOCATION_2], with an order value of EUR 2.7 million, and received an order for the refurbishment of 14 company restaurants of an industrial group, which will be delivered in stages until mid-2027.

Revenue in the Refrigeration and Dishwashing segment grew by 5.0 percent to EUR 14.6 million. Sales of our hood-type dishwashers developed particularly well, supported by the energy-saving heat recovery module that many customers now order as standard. In refrigeration, the market environment remained competitive, and we deliberately refrained from participating in some price-driven tenders in order to protect margins.

The Service and Spare Parts segment once again recorded double-digit growth. Revenue increased by 15.3 percent to EUR 11.3 million. The number of active service contracts rose to 4,860 at the end of the quarter, compared with 4,210 a year earlier. The extension of our own service network to two additional regions in southern Germany and the introduction of guaranteed response times for key accounts made a significant contribution to this development.

Spare parts revenue benefited from the larger installed base and from the new online ordering portal for service partners, through which 41 percent of all spare parts orders were placed in the third quarter. The first-time fix rate of our service technicians improved to 86 percent, mainly because technicians can now check the error history of connected appliances before their visit and bring the right parts with them.

Our Digital Solutions segment, which includes the kitchen management software and the connected appliance platform, increased revenue by 26.5 percent to EUR 4.3 million. Recurring subscription revenue accounted for 78 percent of the segment's revenue. At the end of September, 9,350 appliances were connected to the platform, an increase of 2,100 compared with the end of the previous year. The new HACCP documentation module, which automatically records cooking and cooling temperatures, has been particularly well received by customers in the care sector.

Revenue in Germany rose by 3.0 percent to EUR 36.3 million. International revenue grew by 15.1 percent to EUR 32.1 million, increasing the share of international business from 44 percent to 47 percent. Growth was driven mainly by the Benelux countries, Scandinavia and Austria. In France, where we started direct sales via our own subsidiary at the beginning of the year, revenue doubled from a low base.

The gross margin improved by 0.9 percentage points to 34.1 percent. Material costs fell as a proportion of revenue because stainless steel prices were around 9 percent below the prior-year level on average. This effect was partly offset by higher costs for electronic components and by wage increases of 3.8 percent under the collective agreement that came into force in April.

Personnel expenses rose by 5.6 percent to EUR 21.4 million, mainly due to the collective wage increase and the expansion of the service organisation. Other operating expenses increased by 4.1 percent to EUR 8.7 million, below the growth rate of revenue. Expenses for trade fairs and marketing were lower than in the previous year, when we presented our new product range at two international fairs.

Research and development expenses amounted to EUR 2.9 million, or 4.2 percent of revenue. Our development teams focused on the next generation of induction cooking technology and on further functions for the connected appliance platform.

Overall, EBIT increased to EUR 5.9 million and the EBIT margin rose to 8.6 percent. After the financial result and taxes, net income for the quarter was EUR 4.0 million compared with EUR 3.1 million in the previous year.

Operating cash flow amounted to EUR 6.1 million in the third quarter. After investments of EUR 2.9 million, free cash flow was EUR 3.2 million, a significant improvement on the previous year's figure of EUR 2.1 million. Inventories increased slightly to EUR 41.8 million as we built up stocks of electronic components to secure delivery capability for the fourth quarter.

Net financial debt fell to EUR 11.6 million at 30 September 2026, compared with EUR 15.9 million at the end of 2025. The equity ratio rose to 46.2 percent. Our credit lines of EUR 35 million were drawn to an amount of EUR 8.0 million at the end of the quarter.

At the end of September 2026, [ORG_1] employed 1,112 full-time equivalents, 38 more than a year earlier. Most of the new positions were created in the service organisation and in software development. On 1 September, 31 apprentices and dual students started their training with us, the largest intake to date.

The employee survey conducted in July had a participation rate of 74 percent. Satisfaction with the working atmosphere and with the opportunities for further training improved compared with the last survey in 2024, while the results for internal communication between the sites showed room for improvement. The management board and the works council have agreed on a joint action plan, which will be presented at the works meeting in November.
Investments in the third quarter totalled EUR 2.9 million. The main projects were:
commissioning of the second automated welding line for cooking chambers, investment of EUR 1.1 million
expansion of the central spare parts warehouse by 1,800 pallet spaces, EUR 0.7 million
further roll-out of the new ERP system to the sales subsidiaries, EUR 0.6 million
installation of a photovoltaic system on the roof of the assembly hall with a capacity of 850 kWp, EUR 0.5 million
For the full year 2026, we continue to plan investments of around EUR 11 million.

Energy efficiency is both a sales argument and an obligation for us. In the third quarter, appliances with the highest energy efficiency rating accounted for 63 percent of the revenue generated with new equipment, compared with 52 percent a year earlier. Our customers increasingly ask for documented energy consumption values in tenders, and the connected appliance platform now allows them to evaluate the actual consumption of each appliance in operation.

At our own sites, electricity consumption per unit produced fell by 6 percent compared with the previous year. Once the new photovoltaic system is fully operational, around 22 percent of the electricity required at the assembly plant will be generated on site. In September, we also switched the company car fleet guideline to electric and hybrid vehicles for all new orders. The sustainability report for 2026, which for the first time will be prepared in line with the European reporting standards, is scheduled for publication in April 2027.

The risk situation of [ORG_1] has not changed significantly since the publication of the annual report 2025. The main risks remain the dependence on a small number of suppliers for electronic control units, fluctuations in raw material and energy prices, and the cyclical investment behaviour of our customers in the hotel and catering industry. We address these risks through dual sourcing for critical components, price escalation clauses in large project contracts and the continued expansion of our less cyclical service and software revenue.

The most important opportunities arise from the modernisation needs of public institutions, the growing importance of energy-efficient appliances and the shortage of skilled kitchen staff, which increases demand for automated and connected cooking solutions. We do not currently see any risks that could endanger the continued existence of the company.

On 7 October 2026, [ORG_1] completed the acquisition of a spare parts distributor in Austria with 18 employees and annual revenue of around EUR 4.5 million. The company will be included in the consolidated financial statements from the fourth quarter. The purchase price is in the low single-digit million euro range and was financed from existing liquidity.

The order backlog of EUR 94.6 million provides a solid basis for the fourth quarter, which is traditionally our strongest in terms of revenue. At the same time, we see the following risks and opportunities for the rest of the year:
Supply bottlenecks for certain electronic components could delay deliveries of combi steamers. We have secured most of the required quantities through framework agreements.
The investment programmes announced by several public hospital operators could lead to additional orders, although most of the resulting revenue is only likely to be realised in 2027.
Higher energy prices could dampen investment in the hotel and catering sector, while at the same time increasing demand for our energy-efficient appliances.
The integration of the spare parts business acquired in Austria in October will initially burden earnings with one-off costs of around EUR 0.4 million.

Taking these factors into account, we expect full-year revenue in the upper half of the forecast range of EUR 265 million to EUR 272 million (2025: EUR 251.4 million) and an EBIT margin of between 8.0 and 8.5 percent.
